newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FTC confirms commissioner travels to Brussels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FTC confirms commissioner travels to Brussels.

text.p: Federal Trade Commission member Mary Azcuenaga traveled to Brussels this week, agency officials said Thursday, but speculation she was meeting with the EU competition commissioner could not be confirmed.

A spokeswoman for the FTC said she was unable to confirm speculation that Commissioner Azcuenaga was in Brussels to meet with EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert about a proposed Boeing Co -McDonnell Douglas Corp merger.
Another FTC official said Azcuenaga left for Brussels early this week and was still there Thursday. The official also declined comment on the reason for Azcuenaga's visit.
A Boeing spokeswoman on Wednesday said the company was confident that its proposed merger with McDonnell will be approved by the FTC as early as July 1, and by EU officials soon afterward.
EU Commissioner Van Miert has made it clear that the proposed $14 billion Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger will not be approved as it stands.

European concerns about the proposed deal stem from three exclusive supply pacts Boeing recently signed with three major U.S. airlines for firm orders for over $16 billion. The 20-year exclusive deals were even more lucrative with options included.

News reports surfaced this week that Boeing may be willing to relax terms of its exclusive deals to ease concerns in Europe about the merger. Boeing officials have declined to comment on the report, published in Wednesday's Wall Street Journal.
European leaders have said the exclusive pacts were an obstacle to the approval of the merger because they make it difficult for European aircraft maker Airbus Industrie to compete.
